blocks.content: Quiz: In the video game analogy, what does a Git repository represent?
Tap an option below to answer:
A single save point with a timestamp and description
A save point maps to a commit in Git — a single snapshot. The repository holds all of those commits together.
A save point maps to a commit in Git — a single snapshot. The repository holds all of those commits together.
The game cartridge — the container that holds everything including all saves and history
The repository is the cartridge — it contains the full project, every commit, and the entire history. Commits are the individual save points stored inside it.
The repository is the cartridge — it contains the full project, every commit, and the entire history. Commits are the individual save points stored inside it.
The cloud backup of your game progress
Cloud backup maps to GitHub in this analogy, not the repository itself. A repository lives locally on your machine until you push it to a remote.
Cloud backup maps to GitHub in this analogy, not the repository itself. A repository lives locally on your machine until you push it to a remote.
The folder where you copy and rename your project files
That is what developers do without Git — the manual copy-and-rename approach. A repository replaces that mess with a clean, tracked history.
